newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba telco share offer begins.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba telco share offer begins.

text.p: A public share offer began on Monday for Manitoba Telecom Services Inc, Canada's second last government-owned telephone company, Manitoba's government said.
The share offer was being made exclusively to Manitoba residents at no more than C$13.50 a share until December 14 at 1900 EST/2400 GST.
"One of our main objectives is to ensure Manitobans are offered the opportunity to purchase a majority interest," MTS Minister Glen Findlay said in a statement.
Legislation passed by Manitoba's government last Thursday barred any individual from owning more than 10 percent of MTS.
Trading of MTS shares was scheduled to begin on the Toronto, Montreal and Winnipeg Stock Exchanges on January 7, MTS spokeswoman June Kirby said.
Only Saskatchewan's SaskTel remains as a government owned telco.
Manitoba will issue 70 million common shares in the 90-year-old firm. MTS posted 1995 revenues of C$540 million, versus C$530.8 million in 1994.
